summary: ORS 837.372: Class A violation to operate at/below 400 ft AGL over a fenced/posted critical infrastructure facility (power, water/wastewater, telecom, ports, rail yards, high-hazard dams, correctional facilities) absent owner consent, ownership/occupancy, or FAA-authorized commercial operation. ORS 837.370: bars operating over private property in a manner that intentionally/knowingly/recklessly harasses/annoys. ORS 837.385: vests UAS regulatory authority solely in the legislature, preempting most local ordinances except park takeoff/landing rules (837.387). ORS 837.360/.362: public-body UAS registration/data policies (not private-sector). ORS 837.365: weaponized UAS prohibition.
practical_interpretation_aec_expert: Rely on the 837.372(3)(i) commercial/FAA exemption for critical-infrastructure inspection work, but still get written facility-owner consent when it's easy to obtain — it removes any ambiguity in the field. Because local ordinances are narrowly limited to park takeoff/landing, the main site-specific check for most projects is simply whether the launch/land point is in a park.
practical_interpretation_legal_counsel: Keep FAA authorization and commercial-purpose documentation on file for any critical-infrastructure flight, since the exemption is the operator's burden to establish if challenged. For private-property work, document flight altitude and duration to rebut any claim of intentional or reckless harassment under 837.370.

source_title: Unlawful interference with aircraft, wildfire suppression, law enforcement, or emergency response by unmanned aircraft
uas_topic: Interference with wildfire suppression, law enforcement, emergency response, and manned aircraft
regulated_activity: Directing a laser at an aircraft, crashing into an aircraft, preventing takeoff/landing, or interfering with wildfire suppression/law enforcement/emergency response
summary: Three-tier penalty structure: reckless conduct is a Class A violation; knowing/intentional conduct is a Class A misdemeanor (up to 1 year jail, $6,250 fine); conduct causing death or serious physical injury is a Class A felony (up to 20 years). Covers lasing an aircraft, crashing into an aircraft, preventing aircraft takeoff/landing, or interfering with wildfire suppression, law enforcement, or emergency response operations. A 2025 bill to further elevate penalties (HB 3426) passed the House but died in the Senate at sine die on June 27, 2025 — not current law.
practical_interpretation_aec_expert: Build active-incident awareness into wildfire-season scheduling: check for TFRs and coordinate with incident command before flying anywhere near a fire, law-enforcement operation, or emergency response, since 'interference' is broadly defined and doesn't require actual contact with another aircraft.
practical_interpretation_legal_counsel: Document pre-flight airspace/TFR checks for any job scheduled during fire season, and train field crews that felony-level exposure attaches even without intent to interfere if the conduct is reckless and causes serious injury — this is a strict-enough standard to warrant a written pre-flight checklist item, not just situational judgment.

summary: Drone takeoff/landing is prohibited on all OPRD property and the entire public ocean shore except within designated UAS Operation Areas; a permit pathway remains available for commercial/research use outside those areas. First areas opened without permit requirement beginning August 8, 2026; more sites to be added over time. Overnight-use facilities are categorically closed to UAS takeoff/landing.

practical_interpretation_legal_counsel: Retain the permit approval (or documentation that the site is within a designated Operation Area) in the project file before mobilizing a crew; treat overnight-use facility sites as an absolute exclusion with no permit workaround.
